TBL arrives with the better underlying profile. At five on five the Lightning have taken 59% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in their games, against 53% for VGK, and they allow 2.58 expected goals per 60 minutes to VGK's 2.62. The model expects a tight game, 3.08 expected goals for TBL and 2.93 for VGK. VGK holds the special teams edge, with a power play worth 0.89 expected goals a game to TBL's 0.66, and a penalty kill that allows 0.30 to TBL's 0.53.

Both teams are 4-1-0 in their last five, but the games behind those records differ. TBL has out-chanced every opponent in that stretch, averaging 58% of the expected goals. VGK averages 49%, and its results are ahead of its play: a +17 goal difference against +8.4 expected, driven by finishing and goaltending. Dennis Hildeby (projected) starts for TBL over Andrei Vasilevskiy and is +0.82 in goals saved above expected (how many more goals a goalie stops than an average one facing the same shots) in two games, with +10.06 last season. Carter Hart (projected) is +1.98 this season but was at -4.44 last year.

For TBL, Brandon Hagel has a 43% chance to score and Nikita Kucherov an 82% chance to record a point, and the model flags both as due. For VGK, Mitch Marner brings a six-game point streak (1 goal, 8 assists), and Mark Stone is the likeliest scorer at 31%, though he is flagged as due to cool.
